mutants.reason: Lane 0 is written when wstrb[0]=0 and skipped when wstrb[0]=1, so byte lane 0 of the register is wrong.
At Ec, bvalid is assigned 0 instead of 1, so no write response is ever produced.
During reset, wready resets to 1 instead of 0. This breaks the requirement that wready is 0 in reset and in the cycle ending at R1, so a W transfer could happen at R1.
A write enables every register except the selected one, so the wrong registers change and the targeted one does not.
bvalid is cleared in any cycle without a B handshake, so it drops under bready back-pressure. It is also never cleared by a B transfer, so it is not 0 after Eb.

Reset sets the held-write-data flag to 1, which is a stale held state. After release, wready falls to 0 and the first write never completes. This breaks wready=1 from R1 and the requirement that reset discards held state.
The write data and strobes are latched only when there is no W handshake. When W arrives before AW, the commit uses stale data and strobes, so the wrong value is written.
During reset, awready resets to 1 instead of 0, so awready is high in reset and in the cycle ending at R1. An AW transfer could occur at R1.
Lane 2 is written when wstrb[2]=0 and skipped when wstrb[2]=1, so byte lane 2 of the register is wrong.

r_aw_okay is read only through wr_okay when aw_hs=0, and that case matters only when wr_commit=1 with r_aw_held=1. r_aw_held can become 1 only after an AW transfer, and that same edge loads r_aw_okay from the AW decode, overwriting the reset value. So the reset value is never observed, and no legal stimulus changes any port.

The bvalid set and bresp update happen when there is no commit instead of at Ec. bvalid then rises at the wrong times, so the response is no longer exactly one per write and is not one cycle after Ec.
After the B handshake, bvalid is set to 1 instead of cleared. bvalid never returns to 0, so extra B responses appear and awready/wready stay 0 for the next write.
